# gnomad_missense_constraint_regions_v

Missense constraint regions from the gnomAD v4.1.1 regional missense constraint release
(gs://gcp-public-data--gnomad/papers/2026-rmc), GRCh38. Each transcript's coding span is cut
into one or more regions that differ in how depleted they are of missense variation in
gnomAD, and each region has its observed and expected missense counts: `region_oe` is
observed / expected, and LOWER means more constrained. 40,435 regions on 19,367 transcripts:
one transcript per gene, except six gene symbols that have two, so group by `transcript_id`,
not `gene`. 12,628 of the transcripts have a single region (`n_transcript_regions` = 1): no
regional variation was found, and the row is the whole transcript's missense constraint.
This is the view that answers "which part of this gene is intolerant of missense variation",
which the gene-level views cannot. A region is a genomic interval and spans the introns
between its coding bases, so a variant inside region_start..region_end is not necessarily
coding. Regions of one transcript do not overlap. `is_outlier_transcript` marks the 1,526
transcripts (3,050 rows) the release leaves out of its non-outlier set; treat their values
with caution and exclude them from genome-wide comparisons. `is_high_coverage` is the
source's flag for regions with adequate sequencing coverage. Small table (no partitioning):
filter on `gene`, or on chr and a position range.

## Scan pruning

Clustered on `gene`: an equality on these cuts the bytes billed.

## Columns

| column | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chr` | `INT64` | Chromosome number, X is 23 and Y is 24 |
| `region_start` | `INT64` | First position of the region (GRCh38, inclusive) |
| `region_end` | `INT64` | Last position of the region (GRCh38, inclusive) |
| `gene` | `STRING` | Gene symbol of the transcript (GENCODE v39) |
| `gene_id` | `STRING` | Ensembl gene ID of the transcript (unversioned) |
| `transcript_id` | `STRING` | Ensembl transcript the regions belong to (unversioned) |
| `n_transcript_regions` | `INT64` | Number of regions the transcript has; 1 means no regional variation was found |
| `region_obs` | `INT64` | Observed missense variants in the region |
| `region_exp` | `FLOAT64` | Expected missense variants in the region |
| `region_oe` | `FLOAT64` | Observed / expected missense ratio; lower is more constrained |
| `region_oe_chisq` | `FLOAT64` | Chi-square statistic of the region's observed against expected count |
| `region_oe_chisq_p` | `FLOAT64` | P-value of region_oe_chisq |
| `is_high_coverage` | `BOOL` | The source's high-coverage flag for the region |
| `is_outlier_transcript` | `BOOL` | TRUE where the release leaves the transcript out of its non-outlier set |
| `resource` | `STRING` | Data source identifier, constant 'gnomad' |

## Columns with a small, enumerable set of values

| column | scoped by |
| --- | --- |
| `resource` | — |

## Worked examples

Queries that run against gnomad_missense_constraint_regions_v as written.

### The missense constraint regions of one gene, most constrained first.

```sql
SELECT transcript_id, chr, region_start, region_end, region_obs, region_exp,
       region_oe, region_oe_chisq_p, is_high_coverage, is_outlier_transcript
FROM gnomad_missense_constraint_regions_v
WHERE gene = 'SCN2A'
ORDER BY region_oe
```

### Which constraint region each SCHEMA2 missense variant of one gene falls in. The region join is a position range on the same gene.

```sql
SELECT c.variant, c.hgvsp, c.ac_case, c.ac_ctrl,
       r.region_start, r.region_end, r.region_oe
FROM exome_variant_counts_v c
JOIN gnomad_missense_constraint_regions_v r
  ON r.gene_id = c.gene_id AND r.chr = c.chr
 AND c.pos BETWEEN r.region_start AND r.region_end
WHERE c.chr = 16 AND c.gene = 'SETD1A' AND c.dataset = 'SCHEMA2'
  AND c.consequence = 'missense_variant'
ORDER BY c.pos
```
